newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African shares ended firmer in quiet trade on Thursday, boosted by a firm Dow Jones overnight. Golds retraced most morning losses and ended slighlty weaker.
Dealers said U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's comments on Wednesday were well received by investors.
"The U.S. market has been exceptionally buoyant, taking heart from Greenspan's comments. (Local) industrials have been a touch firmer today on Wall Street," a dealer said.
However, a host of profit warnings from companies including Housewares, Plessey, Sappi and Polifin have dampened sentiment in the market, dealers said.
But local institutions have been buyers at low levels, they said. "Local institutions still see value in industrial equities. They have been buyers at low levels," one said.
Gold shares bounced back after lunch as investors started buying on perception that the gold price had reached bottom.
"Golds have bounced back. People are starting to invest a bit in them," one dealer said.
The market was seen looking to Wall Street for direction on Friday.
The overall index ended up 13.8 points to 7,084.2 points, industrials add 29.2 points to 8,278.0 and golds off 2.6 points to 1,430.1
An asset swap of some 410,000 shares in De Beers boosted the stock which ended up 125 cents to 156 rand in volume worth nearly a 100 million rand.
Anglo shed 250 cents to 275.50 rand, Barlows added a rand to 47 rand and Nedcor jumped 200 cents to 81.50 rand.
Dries gained 60 cents to 46.70 rand, Freegold was 25 cents better at 35.50 rand and Vaal Reefs was a rand weaker at 313 rand.
Near-term equity industrial and all-share futures ended firm on a stronger Wall Street overnight. Gold contracts ended steady to firm on perception that bullion had reached bottom.
Dealers said gold contracts would consolidate at the 1,000 level before ticking up.
The March all-share contract was last at 6,427/40, the industrial contract was at 7,952/57 from 7,929 and the gold contract is at 992/1,008 from 1,005.
